advances: A fixed strictly positive piecewise-affine denominator and the exact actual support graph. Includes old L-contact as a corollary and makes no assertion at a vanishing denominator.

proof:
Use the common unweighted normal reference consisting of the sum of actual and pair-average surface normal marginals. Disintegrate all these surfaces and the old law. At a fixed good normal use one original parity class of positive mass. Its product input bases have integer midpoint in $P$. The common reference form of the surface disintegration ed831700ef36ac67 gives equivalence of each positive conditional law to intrinsic measure on its face. The homogeneous all-ball comparison 26be931a283d8eb3 applies to all pair-average triples, all tight actual target triples and the finite list of self-triples, using the same Radon–Nikodym multiplier on the three members of each triple. Since the large-ball comparison gives positive pair-average conditional mass, alignment by becb3bcb15c98b77 gives a common dimension $m_0$ and tangent space for all positive inputs of the class. On an actual tight output there is positive target mass, and alignment identifies its affine hull with the averaged input affine hull. For $d=1$, take counting reference on the two normals. Every conditional face is then one atom of equal unweighted mass, so no ball comparison is needed.

For $m_0>0$, use baa841580f9a5438 on the self-triples to choose continuous positive intrinsic density representatives in the relative interiors. Midpoints of relative-interior input points in the common tangent space lie in the relative interior of their tight target face. Write $g_-,g_+,g_0$ for the three densities there, or the three masses if $m_0=0$. For positive endpoint weights $F_\pm=g_\pm H_\pm/L_\pm^d$ apply 469dcc371324a1ea with the affine interpolant on the individual endpoint segment having values $L_\pm$. Its midpoint value is $V=(L_-+L_+)/2$. The shared concavity of $H$ and the unequal-radius bound for $g_0$ give, in dimension $m_0>0$,
$$
g_0H_+/V^d\ \ge\ \left[(F_-^{-1/m_0}+F_+^{-1/m_0})/2\right]^{-m_0}.
$$
Here $H_+$ on the left is the positive part of the numerator at the midpoint. In dimension zero the right side is $\min(F_-,F_+)$. In the interval case the same minimum bound follows directly from equal unweighted atom masses and $H(b)\ge (H_-+H_+)/2$. Multiplying by $a^d=(V/L(b))^d$ yields the discounted density comparison against the actual target capacity. Zero endpoint weight has zero lower envelope.

Fix the normal and class. By 8103c38875770e55 the actual support heights extend to a finite concave piecewise affine roof $\widetilde h(z)=\min_j B_j(z)$. For endpoint face points, support contact at the integer midpoint is exactly equality in its midpoint concavity inequality. Couplings with the given marginals on this closed contact relation form a nonempty compact convex set, since it contains the old coupling. Maximize $\int\phi(b)\,d\pi$ there for any smooth uniformly strongly convex $\phi$ on the physical Euclidean space. Partition one optimizer by the least active plane $B_j$ at its output. Both endpoints of that restriction lie in the closed contact cell of $B_j$, since the sum of their nonnegative plane gaps is zero. Any recoupling of its two submarginals stays in the cell and preserves support contact and integer base. Thus the existing restriction is itself an unrestricted strong-surplus optimizer of its own marginals. We use the output parts of the existing optimizer, so their outputs remain disjoint even at positive-mass ties.

The inverse endpoint theorem 0d017e6c3c14b846 gives locally Lipschitz maps from each restricted midpoint to its two endpoints, reconstructing its actual tuple almost everywhere. In the orthogonal coordinates of the common tangent space, fix one output auxiliary level and split by the finitely many input base/offset pairs of the inverse maps. For $m_0>0$ the Lipschitz maps take intrinsic null sets to null sets on these strata, and the marginal bounds imply absolute continuity of the restricted midpoint on this level. Denote its density by $f$. The Lipschitz area formula on each stratum gives $f\le F_i(T_i)|\det DT_i|$ for the two tangent maps $T_i$. Indeed the midpoint mass of a compact subset of the stratum is bounded by the endpoint measure of its image, which is bounded by the area integral with input ceiling. Inner regularity gives the stated density bound. At almost every point of a stratum its density is one. The derivatives of the input base and perpendicular offsets therefore vanish there, and the reconstructed barycentric identity gives $(DT_-+DT_+)/2=I$. The gradient pullback theorem 21fe36cb211350dd, applied to the inverse maps composed with the common surplus gradient, makes the two $DT_i$ similar to symmetric positive semidefinite matrices by the same positive definite tangent Hessian. Taking determinant roots in the two bounds and averaging, the determinant-root versus trace inequality bounds the averaged roots by one. This gives $f\le[(F_-^{-1/m_0}+F_+^{-1/m_0})/2]^{-m_0}$ at the reconstructed tuple. For $m_0=0$ the inverse maps select one tuple per midpoint atom, so its mass is at most each input atom ceiling. In both cases the previous comparison implies that the discounted restricted output is bounded by the actual target on its output part. At a physical base there is at most one on-support affine level, by tight face alignment. The disjoint output parts therefore sum to a single copy of the actual target bound.

The feasible contact couplings with the discounted bound form a compact convex subset. Indeed the bound is tested by $\int f(b)a^d\,d\pi\le\int f\,d\omega$ for every nonnegative continuous output test, and $a$ is continuous and bounded on the compact product. Every strong-surplus maximizer above belongs to this subset. Approximate any finite physical convex test uniformly on the compact range by smooth uniformly strongly convex tests, using convolution and a vanishing quadratic. Its supremum on the subset is at least its old value. For finitely many convex tests, if the compact convex set of differences of their expectations missed the nonnegative orthant, separation by nonnegative coefficients would give one convex test contradicting this supremum bound. Compact finite intersection yields one law in the subset with full convex order above the old law. For this law $\rho=D+E$. The positive part of $\rho-\omega$ is bounded by $E$ because $D\le\omega$, and $a\ge\ell/U$ gives the coarse domination.

Use 9d641a80a1b194d4 to assemble the class couplings. The fixed supports and mass bound give a compact space of finite tuple measures. A countable determining set of continuous tests gives the two marginals, the discounted inequality and convex order, using uniform density on the compact range for convex tests. For fixed normal the actual support contact is a closed constraint, expressed by zero integral of the absolute discrepancy of the normal height from the known support height at the integer midpoint. This discrepancy is Borel in the normal and continuous on the fixed parity product, since the bases are finite. All these constraints are continuous in the candidate measure and Borel in the conditional data. Thus the pointwise solutions assemble without selecting a measurable tangent frame or cell decomposition. Sum over at most $2^n$ parity classes. The entropy theorem on the same fixed-marginal convex-order laws bounds each class error. The map $(m,\Delta)\mapsto m[1-\exp(-d\Delta/m)]$ is the concave homogeneous perspective of a concave function, or equivalently apply its Jensen argument to the union of the classes. This gives the stated total error bound. Use the compact physical martingale theorem ac53fe19fef9ec25 and the same countable Borel selection for a martingale from old to new midpoint in each class. Keeping an old mark and disintegrating the new endpoint tuple over its midpoint then preserves the conditional midpoint mean by the tower property.

The old $L$-contact conclusion uses only the new convex order. The negative of $L$ has the globally finite convex extension $\max_i(-A_i)$, so the new integral of $L$ cannot exceed the old one. The tuple average of the endpoint values has unchanged integral, and concavity gives a nonnegative new gap. If the old gap is zero, the new gap is therefore zero almost everywhere, so $a=1$ and there is no error.

For sharpness the cube fibers form an actual product over $[-1,1]$. Prescribe the full equal face laws at $-1,1$ and let their old pairing have identical continuous points. For any new fixed-marginal pairing of continuous points $X,Y$ their average satisfies
$$
\mathbb E\lVert (X+Y)/2\rVert^2=\mathbb E\lVert X\rVert^2-\tfrac14\mathbb E\lVert X-Y\rVert^2.
$$
Dominating the old midpoint in convex order forces $X=Y$ almost surely. This also holds for the single endpoint atom when $d=1$. The midpoint is at base zero and has $L=1+s$, while both input values are one. Its discounted law is exactly the conditional weighted capacity, and its error is $(1-(1+s)^{-d})\rho$. The old log gap is $m\log(1+s)$, giving equality in the nonlinear logarithmic bound. In the nonlinear power bounds $c_p=m$ and $T_p=T_{p,0}=m(1+s)^p$, so substitution gives equality in both nonlinear comparisons.

statement:
Let $d\ge1$, let $P=\operatorname{conv}(P)\cap\mathbb Z^n$ be finite and nonempty, and let positive convex $d$-fibers be the exact sampled fibers of their canonical hull $C$. Write $\eta$ for their summed boundary measures marked by outward unit normal, with endpoint counting for $d=1$. Let $L=\min_i A_i>0$ on $C$ for finitely many affine functions, with $\ell=\min_C L$ and $U=\max_C L$. For each normal take one finite concave physical numerator $H$ with $W=H_+/L^d$ Borel and bounded on the actual and finitely many pair-average surface ranges. Put $\omega=W\eta$.

Suppose equal-mass endpoints $\gamma_\pm\le\omega$ have an old same-normal coupling $\pi_0$ with integer midpoints on the actual support graph. With $b=(w_-+w_+)/2$ and $a=[L(w_-)+L(w_+)]/(2L(b))$, there is a same-marginal same-normal coupling $\pi$ on the actual midpoint support graph with the following properties. In each normal and original parity class its conditional physical midpoint law $\rho=b_\#\pi$ dominates the old one in full convex order, and its discounted law $D=b_\#(a^d\pi)$ is dominated by one copy of the conditional $\omega$. Writing $E=b_\#((1-a^d)\pi)$ in that class gives $\rho=D+E$, $(\rho-\omega)_+\le E$ and $\rho\le(U/\ell)^d\omega$. For the total marked laws one has $D_{\rm tot}\le 2^n\omega$ and $(\rho_{\rm tot}-2^n\omega)_+\le E_{\rm tot}$. If the common total mass is $m>0$, then
$$
E_{\rm tot}(\mathrm{total})\le m[1-\exp(-d\Delta_0/m)]\le d\Delta_0,
$$
where $\Delta_0$ is the old integrated logarithmic Jensen gap of $L$ on the tuples. At $m=0$ the error is zero. A standard Borel old mark can retain its joint law with the normal and parity and its conditional midpoint mean.

If the old $L$-Jensen gap is zero almost everywhere, the new gap is zero almost everywhere and $\rho$ itself has the one-copy ceiling in each class and the $2^n$ global ceiling. The nonlinear logarithmic bound and the nonlinear power-weighted bounds of the companion entropy theorem are attained on a single class by equal cube fibers at bases $-1,0,1$, $H=1$, $L(z,x)=1+s-s|z|$ for $s>0$, and matching full face laws at the two outside bases with one common facet normal.
title: Exact discounted capacity in concave-projective surface midpoint repair
